# technitium_settings_cache (Data Source)

Reads what `technitium_settings_cache` manages, without managing it.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `cache_failure_record_ttl` (Number) The TTL for caching failed (ServerFailure) answers, so failing name servers aren't queried constantly. Technitium's default is `60`.
- `cache_maximum_entries` (Number) The maximum number of entries the DNS cache can hold. Older entries are removed when the limit is reached.
- `cache_maximum_record_ttl` (Number) The highest TTL a cached record gets, so records expire earlier. Technitium's default is `86400`.
- `cache_minimum_record_ttl` (Number) The lowest TTL a cached record gets, so short-lived records stay cached at least this long. Technitium's default is `10`.
- `cache_negative_record_ttl` (Number) The TTL for caching negative answers that carry no SOA minimum. Technitium's default is `300`.
- `cache_prefetch_eligibility` (Number) The lowest original TTL a record needs to be prefetched.
- `cache_prefetch_trigger` (Number) The remaining TTL below which a query for a cached record starts a prefetch.
- `enable_cache_prefetch` (Boolean) Refresh cached records that are about to expire: a query for a record whose TTL is below `cache_prefetch_trigger` starts a refresh in the background.
- `id` (String) The identifier, as the resource has it.
- `save_cache` (Boolean) Save the DNS cache to disk when the server stops and load it when it starts.
- `serve_stale` (Boolean) Answer from expired cache records when upstream or authoritative name servers can't be reached. Technitium's default is `true`.
- `serve_stale_answer_ttl` (Number) The TTL in seconds of the records in a stale answer, which clients cache it for. Valid range is `0`-`300`; `30` is recommended.
- `serve_stale_max_wait_time` (Number) The milliseconds to wait for the resolver before answering from stale records. `0` answers stale at once. Valid range is `0`-`1800`. Technitium's default is `1800`.
- `serve_stale_reset_ttl` (Number) The seconds a stale record counts as fresh again after a failed refresh, so the resolver doesn't retry it constantly. Valid range is `10`-`900`; `30` is recommended.
- `serve_stale_ttl` (Number) The seconds an expired record stays in the cache to be served stale. 1 to 3 days is recommended, 7 days the most. Technitium's default is `259200`.
